# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhang_2022_linezolid"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhang_2022_linezolid"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2022.1032674> (open access,
  PMC9868619). The article is in volume 13 (2022) and was published online on
  9 January 2023.

Linezolid is a WHO Group A drug for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB).
Zhang et al. developed a population PK model for linezolid 600 mg once daily
in Chinese adults with MDR-TB, used it to estimate individual exposures in a
separate validation cohort, related AUC0-24/MIC to treatment outcome
(threshold 125), and evaluated doses of 300-1400 mg by probability of target
attainment (PTA).

**Read the Errata section before using this model.** It is encoded as printed
in Table 2, and with the printed intercompartmental clearance (Q = 0.9 L/h)
it predicts trough concentrations about half those the paper itself reports.

# Population

The model was developed in 168 participants (1008 plasma samples) of a
prospective multicentre cohort in Jiangsu, Guizhou and Sichuan provinces,
China, 2015-2017 (Zhang 2022 Methods 2.1; Zheng 2021). Participants were
18 to < 70 years old with laboratory-confirmed MDR-TB; critically ill,
pregnant, and HIV-, HBV- or HCV-infected patients were excluded. All received
linezolid 600 mg orally once daily with bedaquiline, a fluoroquinolone and a
background regimen. Blood was sampled after 2 weeks of inpatient treatment,
predose and 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8 h post-dose.

Table 1 (development cohort, median (IQR) or n (%)): age 41 (33-45) years,
weight 53 (47-66) kg, BMI 20 (18-23), 125 (74.4%) male, type 2 diabetes 32
(19.0%). The validation cohort (159 participants, Sichuan, Jiangsu and Henan)
had weight 59 (53-64) kg, 103 (64.8%) male and type 2 diabetes 27 (17.0%),
and was sampled predose, 2 and 6 h post-dose.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Zhang_2022_linezolid")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every value is from Zhang 2022 Table 2. Frontiers typesets decimals without
a leading zero, so the table prints `.9`, `.6`, `.75`, `.1` and `.5`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` | log(2.0 1/h) | Table 2 'Ka (/h)' 2.0, RSD 11.1% |
| `lcl` | log(5.6 L/h) | Table 2 'CL (L/h)' 5.6, RSD 1.6% |
| `lvc` | log(35.8 L) | Table 2 'V d (L)' 35.8, RSD 2.0% |
| `lq` | log(0.9 L/h) | Table 2 'Q (L/h)' .9, RSD 13.7% (see Errata) |
| `lvp` | log(58.6 L) | Table 2 'Vp(L)' 58.6, RSD 13.2% |
| `ltlag` | log(0.6 h) | Table 2 'Tlag(h)' .6, RSD 8.4% |
| `e_wt_cl` | fixed(0.75) | Table 2 'theta (Bodyweight)-CL' .75, no RSD |
| `e_wt_vc` | fixed(1.0) | Table 2 'theta (Bodyweight)-Vd' 1.0, no RSD |
| `e_dis_diab_cl` | 0.1 L/h | Table 2 'theta (Diabetes)-CL' .1, RSD 10.5% |
| `e_dis_diab_vc` | 5.0 L | Table 2 'theta (Diabetes)-Vd' 5.0, RSD 11.1% |
| `etalcl` | 0.045600 | Table 2 IIV CL 21.6 %CV; log(0.216^2 + 1) |
| `etalvc` | 0.057831 | Table 2 IIV Vd 24.4 %CV; log(0.244^2 + 1) |
| `addSd` | 0.5 mg/L | Table 2 'Additional residual (mg/L)' .5, RSD 4.2% |
| Structure | 2-cmt, first-order absorption with lag, linear elimination | Results 3.3; Methods 2.3; Table 2 |
| Weight model | `(WT/70)^e_wt_cl`, `(WT/70)^e_wt_vc` | Form and reference not printed; 70 kg assumed (Assumptions) |
| Diabetes model | `+ e_dis_diab_cl * DIS_DIAB`, `+ e_dis_diab_vc * DIS_DIAB` | Form not printed; additive assumed (Assumptions) |
| Residual error | additive | Results 3.3 'An additive error model was used' |

# Virtual cohorts

Two cohorts of 200 participants each, both on linezolid 600 mg once daily for
15 days. The development cohort (Figure 3) draws weight from a log-normal
distribution with median 53 kg and the Table 1 IQR 47-66 kg, and 19% have type
2 diabetes. The validation cohort (Table 3, Figure 6) uses median 59 kg (IQR
53-64 kg) and 17% type 2 diabetes. Weights are truncated to 35-100 kg.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20230109)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230109)

n_per <- 200
dose_days <- 15
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, 24, by = 0.25),
  seq(336, 360, by = 0.25)
)))

make_cohort <- function(n, wt_median, wt_q1, wt_q3, p_diab, cohort, id_offset = 0L) {
  sdlog <- (log(wt_q3) - log(wt_q1)) / (2 * qnorm(0.75))
  subj <- tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    WT = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(wt_median), sdlog)), 35), 100),
    DIS_DIAB = rbinom(n, 1, p_diab),
    cohort = cohort
  )
  dose <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = 24 * (seq_len(dose_days) - 1)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 600, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

events <- bind_rows(
  make_cohort(n_per, 53, 47, 66, 0.19, "Development", id_offset = 0L),
  make_cohort(n_per, 59, 53, 64, 0.17, "Validation", id_offset = n_per)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

events |>
  distinct(id, cohort, WT, DIS_DIAB) |>
  group_by(cohort) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    `WT median (kg)` = round(median(WT), 1),
    `WT IQR (kg)` = paste(round(quantile(WT, c(0.25, 0.75)), 1), collapse = "-"),
    `Type 2 diabetes (%)` = round(100 * mean(DIS_DIAB), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated cohort covariates.")
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhang_2022_linezolid"))
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("cohort", "WT", "DIS_DIAB"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

# Replicate Figure 3 (steady-state VPC, development cohort)

Figure 3 is a VPC of the development cohort after 2 weeks of treatment. The
points overlaid below are the median of the simulated data, read by the
maintainers from the centre of the shaded 95% confidence band of Figure 3
(approximately; the figure has no gridlines below 3 mg/L).

```{r figure-3}
fig3_median <- tibble(
  tad = c(1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 24),
  Cc = c(7.4, 7.8, 6.9, 6.1, 5.5, 2.3)
)

vpc <- sim |>
  filter(cohort == "Development", time >= 336) |>
  mutate(tad = time - 336) |>
  group_by(tad) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    Q50 = quantile(sim, 0.50),
    Q95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(tad, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_point(data = fig3_median, aes(tad, Cc), colour = "firebrick", size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 6)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Linezolid concentration (mg/L)",
    title = "Steady state (day 15), development-cohort covariates",
    caption = paste(
      "Line and band: simulated median and 5th-95th percentiles (with residual error).",
      "Points: simulated median read from Zhang 2022 Figure 3.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  )
```

```{r figure-3-ratio}
fig3_ratio <- vpc |>
  inner_join(fig3_median, by = "tad") |>
  mutate(ratio = Q50 / Cc)
knitr::kable(
  fig3_ratio |>
    select(tad, Q50, Cc, ratio) |>
    mutate(across(c(Q50, Cc, ratio), ~ round(.x, 2))) |>
    rename(
      "Time after dose (h)" = tad,
      "Simulated median (mg/L)" = Q50,
      "Figure 3 median (mg/L)" = Cc,
      "Ratio" = ratio
    ),
  caption = "Simulated median vs. the Figure 3 simulated median."
)
```

The packaged model peaks at about
`r round(fig3_ratio$ratio[fig3_ratio$tad == 2], 1)` times the Figure 3 median
at 2 h, and its 24 h trough is about
`r round(fig3_ratio$ratio[fig3_ratio$tad == 24], 1)` times the Figure 3
value. The Errata section discusses why.

# Steady-state exposure versus Table 3 (PKNCA)

Table 3 reports the individual (Bayesian posthoc) Cmax, Cmin and AUC0-24 of
the validation cohort. These are compared with a PKNCA analysis of the
day-15 dosing interval (336-360 h) of the simulated validation cohort.

```{r pknca}
conc_ss <- sim |>
  filter(cohort == "Validation", !is.na(Cc), time >= 336) |>
  mutate(treatment = "600 mg QD") |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

dose_ss <- events |>
  filter(cohort == "Validation", evid == 1) |>
  mutate(treatment = "600 mg QD") |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_ss, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_ss, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 336, end = 360,
  cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~cmin, ~auclast,
  "600 mg QD", 16.2, 2.0, 108.3
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", cmin = "mg/L", auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Simulated (median) vs. Zhang 2022 Table 3 (validation cohort, median).",
    "* differs from the reference by more than 20%."
  )
)
```

Cmax and AUC0-24 agree with Table 3 within about 13%; AUC follows from CL
alone (AUC = dose/CL at steady state), so this confirms the clearance and its
weight scaling. Cmin is about half the Table 3 value, which is the known
deviation described in the Errata.

```{r gate-table3}
nca_med <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "auclast")) |>
  group_by(PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")
med <- setNames(nca_med$median, nca_med$PPTESTCD)

stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-transcribed CL, dose or weight exponent moves the
  # steady-state AUC median by tens of percent. Simulated median is ~+13%.
  abs(100 * (med[["auclast"]] / 108.3 - 1)) < 25,
  abs(100 * (med[["cmax"]] / 16.2 - 1)) < 25,
  # Known deviation, pinned so it cannot change silently: with the printed
  # Q = 0.9 L/h the median trough is ~1.0 mg/L against the paper's 2.0 mg/L.
  med[["cmin"]] > 0.6, med[["cmin"]] < 1.4
)
```

# Readings of Q and the reference weight

Table 2 prints Q as `.9` L/h and does not state the reference weight. The
table below re-runs the validation cohort under four readings: Q of 0.9 L/h
(as printed) or 9 L/h, and a reference weight of 70 kg (as packaged) or the
development-cohort median of 53 kg. Because both weight exponents act on
`WT / 70`, the 53 kg reading is reproduced exactly by passing `WT * 70 / 53`;
the diabetes shifts are additive and are unaffected.

Figure 6 PTA values are from the Results text (section 3.6) and, under linear
PK, convert to probabilities that the 600 mg AUC0-24 exceeds a threshold:
1400 mg reaching AUC/MIC 125 at MIC 1 mg/L in 93.1% means
P(AUC600 >= 53.6) = 93.1%, and 300 mg at MIC 0.25 mg/L (74.2%) and 1200 mg at
MIC 1 mg/L (68.6%) both mean P(AUC600 >= 62.5). The probabilities are computed
for both the day-1 and the day-15 AUC0-24.

```{r readings}
auc_trap <- function(time, conc) sum(diff(time) * (head(conc, -1) + tail(conc, -1)) / 2)

val_events <- events |> filter(cohort == "Validation")
readings <- tidyr::crossing(q = c(0.9, 9), ref_wt = c(70, 53))

reading_summary <- function(q, ref_wt) {
  ev <- val_events |> mutate(WT = WT * 70 / ref_wt)
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, params = c(lq = log(q)), returnType = "data.frame")
  per_id <- s |>
    group_by(id) |>
    summarise(
      auc_d1 = auc_trap(time[time <= 24], Cc[time <= 24]),
      auc_ss = auc_trap(time[time >= 336], Cc[time >= 336]),
      cmax_ss = max(Cc[time >= 336]),
      cmin_ss = Cc[time == 360],
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  tibble(
    q = q, ref_wt = ref_wt,
    cmax_ss = median(per_id$cmax_ss),
    cmin_ss = median(per_id$cmin_ss),
    auc_ss = median(per_id$auc_ss),
    auc_d1 = median(per_id$auc_d1),
    p536_d1 = 100 * mean(per_id$auc_d1 >= 53.6),
    p625_d1 = 100 * mean(per_id$auc_d1 >= 62.5),
    p536_ss = 100 * mean(per_id$auc_ss >= 53.6),
    p625_ss = 100 * mean(per_id$auc_ss >= 62.5)
  )
}

reading_tab <- bind_rows(Map(reading_summary, readings$q, readings$ref_wt))

bind_rows(
  reading_tab |>
    mutate(Reading = paste0("Q ", q, " L/h, ", ref_wt, " kg reference",
                            ifelse(q == 0.9 & ref_wt == 70, " (packaged)", ""))),
  tibble(Reading = "Zhang 2022 (Table 3; Results 3.6)",
         cmax_ss = 16.2, cmin_ss = 2.0, auc_ss = 108.3,
         p536_d1 = 93.1, p625_d1 = 74.2)
) |>
  select(Reading, cmax_ss, cmin_ss, auc_ss, auc_d1, p536_d1, p625_d1, p536_ss, p625_ss) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 1))) |>
  rename(
    "Cmax ss (mg/L)" = cmax_ss,
    "Cmin ss (mg/L)" = cmin_ss,
    "AUC0-24 ss (mg*h/L)" = auc_ss,
    "AUC0-24 day 1 (mg*h/L)" = auc_d1,
    "P(AUC d1 >= 53.6) %" = p536_d1,
    "P(AUC d1 >= 62.5) %" = p625_d1,
    "P(AUC ss >= 53.6) %" = p536_ss,
    "P(AUC ss >= 62.5) %" = p625_ss
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Validation-cohort medians and AUC exceedance under four readings (no residual error).")
```

```{r gate-readings}
q9 <- reading_tab |> filter(q == 9, ref_wt == 70)
q09 <- reading_tab |> filter(q == 0.9, ref_wt == 70)
stopifnot(
  # The Q = 9 L/h reading recovers the Table 3 trough (2.0 mg/L) and the
  # printed reading does not; both are medians over 200 subjects.
  abs(q9$cmin_ss / 2.0 - 1) < 0.3,
  q09$cmin_ss / 2.0 < 0.7,
  # Q does not change the steady-state AUC (it is dose/CL for both).
  abs(q9$auc_ss / q09$auc_ss - 1) < 0.05
)
```

# Typical-value profile

```{r typical}
typ_events <- rxode2::et(amt = 600, ii = 24, addl = dose_days - 1, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(336, 360, by = 0.1), cmt = "central")
typ <- bind_rows(
  lapply(c(53, 70), function(w) {
    rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = typ_events,
                    params = c(WT = w, DIS_DIAB = 0), returnType = "data.frame") |>
      mutate(WT = paste(w, "kg"))
  })
)

ggplot(typ, aes(time - 336, Cc, colour = WT)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose on day 15 (h)", y = "Linezolid concentration (mg/L)",
       colour = "Body weight",
       title = "Typical steady-state profile, no type 2 diabetes")

# Closed-form check: steady-state AUC over one interval is dose/CL.
typ_auc <- typ |> group_by(WT) |> summarise(auc = auc_trap(time, Cc), .groups = "drop")
cl_typ <- 5.6 * (c(53, 70) / 70)^0.75
stopifnot(all(abs(typ_auc$auc / (600 / cl_typ) - 1) < 0.01))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Reference weight (assumed 70 kg).** Table 2 gives fixed allometric
  exponents (0.75 on CL, 1.0 on Vd) but no reference weight and no covariate
  equation. The maintainers used the standard 70 kg. The development-cohort
  median of 53 kg is the other candidate. With a 53 kg reference, typical CL
  for a given weight would be 23% higher and the typical volume 32% higher;
  the "Readings" table above shows both.
- **Diabetes effect form (assumed additive).** Table 2 gives theta(Diabetes)
  of 0.1 on CL and 5.0 on Vd without the equation. Read as an exponential
  (exp(5) = 148-fold), multiplicative (5-fold) or fractional (1 + 5 = 6-fold)
  effect, 5.0 is implausible for a volume, so both coefficients are encoded
  as additive shifts in the parameter's units (CL + 0.1 L/h, Vc + 5.0 L).
  The additive CL shift is about 2% of the typical CL.
- **IIV.** Table 2 reports IIV as %CV; it is converted to log-normal variance
  as omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1). The CL row is labelled '(L/h)' but sits under
  'Variation of parameters between individuals' with the Vd row labelled
  '%CV', so it is read as %CV. No IIV on Ka, Q, Vp or Tlag is reported.
- **Bioavailability.** Only oral data were modelled; Table 2 labels CL and Vd
  without '/F'. The parameters are apparent (oral) values, and no
  bioavailability term is included.
- **Cohorts.** Weight is log-normal with the Table 1 median and IQR, and
  type 2 diabetes is independent of weight. Age, sex and BMI are not in the
  model.

# Errata

The model is encoded exactly as printed in Table 2. Several of the paper's
own results cannot be reproduced from those values:

- **Trough concentration.** Table 3 reports a posthoc median Cmin of 2.0 mg/L
  (IQR 1.5-2.3) in the validation cohort. The packaged model gives about
  1.0 mg/L. The Figure 2 goodness-of-fit plots also place population-predicted
  troughs at roughly 1.3-2.3 mg/L. A Q of 9 L/h, rather than the printed
  `.9`, recovers the Table 3 trough (see "Readings") without changing CL or
  the steady-state AUC. Frontiers typesets decimals without a leading zero,
  so a lost digit would look like this, but the paper does not correct it
  and the maintainers have kept the printed value.
- **Figure 3 VPC.** The simulated median in Figure 3 peaks at about
  7.8 mg/L and falls almost mono-exponentially to about 2.3 mg/L at 24 h.
  Neither Q reading reproduces this: a 35.8 L central volume with
  Ka = 2.0 /h after 600 mg gives a typical peak of 10-18 mg/L, consistent with
  the Table 3 Cmax of 16.2 mg/L but not with the VPC.
- **Figure 6 PTA.** Under linear PK the Results-text PTA values imply that
  only 26-31% of the simulated population had a 600 mg AUC0-24 below
  62.5 mg*h/L, i.e. a median AUC0-24 well below the Table 3 steady-state
  median of 108.3. No steady-state reading reproduces this; a day-1
  AUC0-24 with Q = 9 L/h and a 53 kg reference comes closest. The paper does
  not state which AUC was used in the PTA simulation.
- **Steady-state AUC and Cmax** reproduce within about 13% of Table 3 with the
  packaged model, so CL, its weight scaling and the central volume are
  consistent with the paper.

No correction notice for this article was found on the journal page or in
Europe PMC as of 2026-10-16.
